questions.stem: What is the formula for concentration in mol/dm³?
questions.explanation: Concentration (mol/dm³) = Number of moles / Volume (dm³). This gives the number of moles of solute per dm³ of solution.

questions.stem: How many moles of NaOH are in 500 cm³ of a 2 mol/dm³ solution?
questions.explanation: Moles = Concentration x Volume. Convert 500 cm³ to 0.5 dm³. Moles = 2 x 0.5 = 1 mole.

questions.stem: 0.1 moles of HCl is dissolved in 250 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration?
questions.explanation: 250 cm³ = 0.25 dm³. Concentration = Moles / Volume = 0.1 / 0.25 = 0.4 mol/dm³.

questions.stem: How do you convert concentration from g/dm³ to mol/dm³?

options.text: Divide the concentration in g/dm³ by the Mr
Add the Mr to the concentration

questions.explanation: To convert from g/dm³ to mol/dm³, divide by the Mr. This is because moles = mass / Mr, so the same relationship applies to concentrations.

questions.stem: What volume of a 0.5 mol/dm³ solution contains 0.2 moles of solute?
A solution of NaOH has a concentration of 40 g/dm³. What is this in mol/dm³? [Mr of NaOH = 40]
questions.explanation: Concentration in mol/dm³ = Concentration in g/dm³ / Mr = 40 / 40 = 1 mol/dm³.

questions.stem: In a titration, 25 cm³ of a 0.1 mol/dm³ NaOH solution is used. How many moles of NaOH is this?
questions.explanation: 25 cm³ = 0.025 dm³. Moles = Concentration x Volume = 0.1 x 0.025 = 0.0025 moles.
